title: Day templates & smoother history
highlights: Create and manage reusable day layouts under Settings → Training plan → Day templates—edit rounds, exercises, stretches, and cardio the same way you Edit Day.

When you Apply a template on Edit Day, choose how it merges: replace the whole day, append as new rounds, or replace one round. Single-round finishers default to append so they don’t wipe the rest of your day.
Logging a past workout from Weekly is easier to leave—Back returns to that week day, then to Weekly, instead of walking through start and complete screens.
Workout checkboxes, menus, and chevrons have larger tap targets so they’re easier to hit on the phone.

title: Gym machines & smarter progression
highlights: On Training plan → Equipment, choose Typical gym set or pick specific stations (leg press, lat pulldown, smith, and more) instead of one generic Machines option. Plans only suggest machines you actually have. If you already had Machines selected, you now have the full typical set.
Progression suggestions and More details use your Library default reps, not a leftover catalog target—so a 10-rep Library default is what you log against, even if the catalog still says 8.
Progression lives under Settings → Training plan. Training plan and Device & timers sections now collapse so you can scan the page without opening everything at once.
During a workout, More details lets you edit Library default reps and weight, including picking from your weight inventory.

title: Simpler strength exercises
highlights: Moves like Bent Knee Calf Raise, lunges, and Sumo Squats are one exercise now—bodyweight or with weights. Log weight on the set (or leave it blank) instead of picking a separate “dumbbell” or “barbell” version.
If you used an older weighted version before, your history and plans still line up with the new name automatically.
Your Library weight defaults still pre-fill the next time you do that move, just like before.
On Health → Exercises, Exercise over time shows weight in tooltips and Sessions when you logged it—bodyweight days still show reps and sets only.
